# GitHub Actions workflows

The inventory is generated from the workflow YAML. Run
`node scripts/workflow-inventory.mjs --write` after changing triggers or jobs.
`--check` verifies that both the table and the merge queue listener list match
the YAML. A conditional job can run when its expressions and dependencies
allow it. Required and shadow contexts use the merge queue ruleset test.

| Workflow file | What it does | Triggers | Required repo secrets |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ci-scorecard.yml` | D5603: report the last 24 hours of CI and queue metrics in the job summary and update one comment on #5600. D5973: upload one classified row per merge-group candidate as the `ci-scorecard-candidates` artifact. | Daily cron and manual dispatch | None beyond the job's GitHub token. |
| `channel-worker-contracts.yml` | Focused D684 messaging, foundation and frontend reply contracts with mocked provider I/O; supplements the root build and full drift gate | PR to `main` touching channel Worker contracts | none (`contents: read`) |
| `github-alerts.yml` | D6387 uses a five-minute schedule and exact-attempt dispatches to open or update GitHub repair issues. See [workflow failure reporting](../../documentation/operations/WORKFLOW_FAILURE_ISSUES_6387.md). Other checks send GitHub health alerts to one Slack channel (`scripts/github-alerts.mjs`, rules in `scripts/lib/githubAlerts.mjs`). `main-red`: every 15 minutes, the latest finished CI run on a push to `main` failed (a poll: WF-4 keeps `workflow_run` out). `queue`: the Actions queue backed up (default 40 queued runs or the oldest waiting 45 min). `future-clock`: nightly, the eight CI test parts run with every test process's clock 7 days ahead: libfaketime moves the operating system's clock, so `Date`, SQLite's `datetime('now')` and a script's `date` agree, `scripts/future-clock.mjs` carries it into children started with their own env, and `scripts/future-clock-check.mjs` fails the job first if any of the three did not move (D5398; moving `Date` alone gave 817 false failures on 2026-11-10), so a date-bound test (D5052, D5039) is reported before its date breaks `main`. Each of `main-red` and `queue` is one open issue titled `[alert] ...`: Slack hears only when it opens and when it closes. A reporter error fails its job | cron `2-57/5 * * * *` (workflow failures), cron `*/15 * * * *` (main red), hourly cron `7 * * * *` (queue), nightly cron `23 2 * * *` (future clock), manual dispatch with `check` | `SLACK_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_URL` (a Slack incoming webhook; without it the issues still open and close and the job warns). Optional variables `QUEUE_ALERT_QUEUED`, `QUEUE_ALERT_OLDEST_MIN`, and `QUEUE_ALERT_IGNORE_BEFORE` (an ISO date: queued runs created before it are left out of the count and the oldest age, and the open alert issue says how many and the cutoff; an invalid date fails the job and ignores nothing; #6463). `GITHUB_TOKEN`: `contents: read`, `issues: write`, `actions: read`, and `checks: read` on the workflow-failure job |

## The merge queue (#4107)

`main` merges through GitHub's merge queue. A queued pull request is tested
on a temporary `gh-readonly-queue/main/…` branch, which is main plus every PR
ahead of it in the queue, through the `merge_group` event, and it merges only
when main's required checks pass there. A PR that no longer merges cleanly
with the ones ahead of it is taken out of the queue with the reason.

| Required check | Workflow | Under `merge_group` |
|---|---|---|
| test:drift (full suite) | `ci.yml` | runs, with the `suite (<part>)` jobs it needs; the parts run in parallel (D4130) |
| worker (typecheck) | `ci.yml` | runs |
| frontend (build) | `ci.yml` | runs |
| api ↔ worker drift | `ci.yml` | runs |
| applied migrations unchanged | `migration-immutability.yml` | diffs against `merge_group.base_sha` |
| scan | `gitleaks.yml` | scans `merge_group.base_sha..head_sha` |
- `archive-observer-deploy.yml` · D5676: type-checks, packages and deploys the isolated archive observer once enabled · main pushes touching observer or tail source, manual · `ARCHIVE_OBSERVER_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `ARCHIVE_OBSERVER_DEPLOY_ENABLED`
- `merge-control-deploy.yml` · D5618: independent SQLite DO/Queue control Worker; main only and disabled until explicitly enabled · main pushes touching Merge Control, manual · `MERGE_CONTROL_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`; `MERGE_CONTROL_DEPLOY_ENABLED`
- `pr-overlap.yml` · D5616: advisory overlap comments and parent summary; no PR code executes. D5580: hunk risk classes, per-PR evidence and a dated 30-day snapshot artifact · hourly and manual · `actions: read`, `checks: read`, `contents: read`, `issues: write`, `pull-requests: write`
- `claims-reaper.yml` · D5617: comments once per expired atomic task claim, never deletes refs · hourly and manual · `contents: read`, `issues: write`

The generated inventory above lists the workflows that listen for `merge_group`.
Previews, reviews, comments and deployment stay outside the queue. The deploy starts on a push
to `main`. During the D5606 shadow phase, `ci / fast` and `landing gate` also
run in the queue. There the fast job runs only the migration and drift
checkers loaded from the trusted base. Its gitleaks, typecheck and build
steps are skipped in the queue, because the required `scan`,
`worker (typecheck)` and `frontend (build)` jobs run the same commands on the
same candidate (D7108). So in the queue, `ci / fast` and `landing gate` do
not reflect typecheck, build or secret-scan results, and the D5606 shadow
comparison covers only migrations, drift and the suite there. Before the
D5606 cutover makes either check required, or the `frontend`, `worker` or
`scan` jobs are deleted, those six skips and the verdict's `merge_group`
skip branch must be reverted; `landing_gate_5606.test.mjs` fails otherwise.
On PRs and pushes, fast runs every step. Dependency
audits and routing docs run on PRs and pushes, and the LFS check runs on PRs.
The `worker-*` suite parts skip the frontend install and the SPA build, which
only the `frontend-*` parts and `rest` need (D7108).

The two aggregators run on `always()` so a failing dependency cannot make
either check report as skipped. `landing gate` requires a passing fast
verdict and follows the same suite rule as `test:drift (full suite)`.
Advisory step failures can make the fast job red while its required
verdict passes. `frontend/test/merge_queue_ci_4107.test.mjs` tracks the
active ruleset in `REQUIRED` and the shadow check in `SHADOW`.

The queue was switched on on 2026-11-02 (#4107). The ruleset lets the Admin
role bypass it, so an admin's plain Merge skips the queue and its checks: use
**Merge when ready**, which adds the pull request to the queue.

## When a workflow starts failing

1. Open the failing run in the GitHub UI **immediately** — the per-job
   log API only retains blobs for ~15 minutes; after that you only have
   the in-browser log view.
2. If the job died in 1-3 seconds with empty step logs, the cause is
   usually one of:
   - A required secret is missing from the repo settings (see the workflow notes below).
   - The repo or org disabled GitHub Actions, or hit a billing/spending limit.
   - An "Allowed actions" policy blocks a referenced action.
   - The runner image is broken (rare, GitHub status page will say so).
3. If the job ran but a step failed, look at the first `##[error]` line.
4. **`backup-d1.yml` / `dr-drill.yml` — missing or wrong Cloudflare secret**
   The "Preflight — assert required secrets are set" step fails immediately
   with:
   ```
   Required repo secret(s) are missing or empty: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
   ```
   or (if the secret is set but wrangler still rejects it mid-run):
   ```
   ✘ [ERROR] In a non-interactive environment, it's necessary to set a
   CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN environment variable for wrangler to work.
   ```
   Fix: go to **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository
   secret** and add/update both `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and
   `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` as **repository** secrets (not environment-scoped —
   these jobs declare no `environment:`, so environment-scoped secrets are
   invisible). The token must have **D1 export/read + R2 object write** scopes;
   a `Workers Scripts: Edit`-only token is not sufficient.
5. For dependency-audit failures, run `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=critical`
   locally in `frontend/` or `cloudflare-worker/`, and
   `pip-audit -r requirements.txt` for Python.
6. For gitleaks failures, run `gitleaks detect --config=.gitleaks.toml --source=.`
   locally and either fix the leak or add it to the allowlist in
   `.gitleaks.toml`.

## Action version pinning policy

Every action is pinned to a **full commit SHA with a trailing `# vN`
comment**, regardless of publisher — `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5… # v7`,
`github/codeql-action/analyze@cdf488f5… # v4`. (This paragraph used to say
major-version tags for GitHub-published actions; that had not been the
practice here for some time.) The comment says which release the SHA is,
the SHA says what actually runs.

**Container images under `container:` follow the same rule, by digest plus
a trailing `# <version>` comment** — `mirror.gcr.io/semgrep/semgrep@sha256:34ab619b… #
1.176.1`. A moving tag is a floating ref: `:latest` is banned here for the
same reason `@main` is, and it had already changed a Semgrep finding count
with no repo change twice before it was pinned (D170). The registry may
change and the digest may not: Semgrep's image is pulled through
`mirror.gcr.io` because Docker Hub rate-limited the shared runners
(GOTCHAS.md, "Static analysis").

Do NOT use floating refs like `@main`, `:latest`, or unreleased majors
(e.g. `@v5` for `actions/checkout` doesn't exist as of 2026-05-21).

## Meeting bot image (#2586, D886 B8)

`meeting-bot-image.yml` tests image naming/deployment isolation, builds a labelled
scratch fixture, dry-runs the independent host configuration, then builds and
boots the real runtime without provider network access. The native SDK must
load. PR jobs never log into a registry. A manual main run can publish a
commit-tagged GHCR image with the job-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN`; its digest is
recorded in the job summary. The bot deploy workflow builds its own image for
Wrangler's registry and never runs site D1 migrations.

## Independent meeting bot release (D886 B8)

`meeting-bot-deploy.yml` handles main bot changes and manual main dispatch,
behind the owner-set `MEETING_BOT_DEPLOY_ENABLED` Actions variable. It uses
`MEETING_BOT_CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and deploys only the preview and production bot hosts, in that order.
`meeting-bot-image.yml` validates the real image/native load and bot config
dry runs on PRs. Site deployment never builds or publishes a bot image.

D1165 (#3072, PR #3230): the form/lightbox workflow keeps all focused checks,
guards, the root build and full drift. Its job has the same 60-minute bound as
the main CI gate: the prior 30-minute limit cancelled a run during final lint.
No trigger, permission, secret or check changes.

D5609 (#5609): `ci.yml` and `github-alerts.yml` consume generated suite-plan
artifacts and compact name outputs. Missing main timings use equal weights.
D7108 part 2: in the merge queue `ci.yml` runs no `plan` job; each suite part
writes the equal-weight plan itself (`--plan --equal-weights`) from its commit.

D5675: the meeting-bot deploy verifies the exact deployed preview revision and signed synthetic callback before normal production promotion; missing preflight stops promotion.
`release-rehearsal.yml` (D5501) checks release admission fixtures and profiles
its exact Worker candidate on a disposable Linux runner using isolated workerd.
It uses synthetic queue responses and has no production credentials.

The third reads `email_send_log`, which the `waitUntil` send writes before enqueueing and the queue consumer marks `sent` only once Gmail accepted the message — so a row stuck at `queued` is the silent-send failure, and **without this verdict the probe would pass on a login that answers 202 and delivers nothing**. It still does **not** prove the mail ARRIVED (acceptance is not an inbox, and it never follows the link), and says so in every report; `magic-link-probe.yml` remains the only check that can close #168. Cron `0 */4 * * *`, **deliberately 30 minutes offset** from that probe: both request a link for the same address, and if this one fired inside the mailbox probe's polling window the mailbox probe would accept THIS probe's email as its own and pass without proving its own mail arrived. Until `MAGIC_PROBE_EMAIL` is set the job fails COULD NOT RUN, which is distinct from a failing sign-in and says so.

Until all four are set the job fails with NOT CONFIGURED and task #168 stays unverified.

- `migration-immutability.yml` · Fails when a migration already on the base is edited, deleted, renamed or retyped — the runner never re-runs an applied file, so such an edit reaches only databases built from the files afterwards, and they then disagree with production. Eight applied migrations drifted this way before it existed (D269). Runs `scripts/migration-immutability-gate.mjs` against a pull request's base branch, and on a push to main against the commit main pointed at before the push, because six of the eight arrived by direct push, and in the merge queue against the main commit the queue built the entry on (`merge_group.base_sha`, #4107). Its own workflow rather than a `ci.yml` job: `ci.yml` cancels an in-progress run on main when the next push lands, and a cancelled push's range would never be checked, so here only pull-request runs cancel. There is no bypass · push/PR to `main`; `merge_group` · none (uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` only, `contents: read`)
- `post-deploy-smoke.yml` · Live SPA smoke check — key routes on both Worker custom domains, `axal.vc` + `app.axal.vc`, return the rendered SPA shell (200 + `<div id="root">` + `/assets/*.js`) **with the static security headers `docs/_headers` sets** (HSTS, nosniff, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`), not a blank page or JSON 404. This probe is the evidence a host updated, and its header checks are the live answer to `documentation/architecture/UNRESOLVED_ITEMS.md` U10. A second, warning-only step runs `scripts/check-ai-credits-live.mjs` (D755): the public plans-and-packs read and `/plans-and-pricing` · manual dispatch, 6-hourly cron · none (plain public HTTPS).
- `pr-overlap.yml` · D5616: advisory overlap comments and parent summary; no PR code executes. D5580: hunk risk classes, per-PR evidence and a dated 30-day snapshot artifact · hourly and manual · `actions: read`, `checks: read`, `contents: read`, `issues: write`, `pull-requests: write`
- `pr-preview.yml` · One Worker per pull request — `studioos-pr-<number>` on workers.dev — built from the PR's frontend and deployed from `wrangler.pr-preview.toml` (no bindings: the SPA build only, `/api/*` a 404, no production data in reach), its URL kept in one sticky comment; deleted when the PR closes. Its `login-e2e` job then runs `frontend/tests/e2e/google_popup_signin.spec.js` (D722, "Continue with Google" through Google's window on /login) against that preview in Playwright's Chromium; the spec stubs Google's script and every `/api/auth/google/*` route, so the job holds no secret. The same job runs `frontend/tests/e2e/integrations.spec.js` (D753, #1992: the Connectors hub, its filter menu, one connector's page and the 390px check), which stubs every `/api/*` call it makes. Same-repository PRs only, never Dependabot. Why not Workers preview URLs: none exist for a Worker that implements a Durable Object (`documentation/architecture/DECISIONS.md` D36) · PR opened / synchronize / reopened / ready_for_review / closed. Drafts get no preview: the first deploy is when the PR is marked ready (D4130); cleanup on close runs for every PR. A separate job deletes the same-repository source branch on merges into `main` if its tip still matches the merged PR and no open PR uses it. Protected, default, task-claim, and merge-queue branches are kept. This job uses only the built-in token (`contents: write`, `pull-requests: read`). · `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (Workers Scripts:Edit — the deploy token already has it), `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
- `prompt-eval-gate.yml` · D1519 (#3771): fails a pull request that changes a deck prompt (`cloudflare-worker/src/services/decks/prompts/`) unless `documentation/product/ELEMENT_EVAL.md` records the new prompts hash (the element eval was re-run, D1518) or the PR carries the owner's `prompt-eval-waiver` label. Runs `scripts/check-prompt-eval.mjs`; `labeled` and `unlabeled` re-run it · every PR (opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled) · none (`contents: read`)
- `record-page-contracts.yml` · D696 renderer, action dispatch and persona export with mutation/restoration, static guards, root build then full drift with explicit exit code · PR to `main` touching record/persona contracts · none (`contents: read`)
- `release-alpha-rename.yml` · One-off: gives the releases #2655 left without a stage suffix (v1.0.1 to v8.3.26) their `-alpha` tag on the same commit and moves each release onto it; drafts change name only. Dry run by default; old tags kept unless asked · manual dispatch only · none (`GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: write`)
- `release-draft.yml` · Maintains daily drafts from the complete first-parent history of main; active month totals, monthly zero-based week (0–4) and active day (1–31) counters, UTC. Published daily tags/releases stay fixed; missing days are backfilled and only matching drafts refresh · push to `main`; manual dispatch · none (`GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: write`)
- `release-published.yml` · When the owner publishes a release, dispatches `cloudflare-worker-deploy.yml` on `main`, so the build picks up the new tag and the version beside the logo shows it; never deploys the tag's own commit · release published · none (`GITHUB_TOKEN` with `actions: write`)
- `release-rehearsal.yml` · D5501: validates release-admission fixtures against synthetic queue responses, builds the frontend, and checks the prepared Worker on an isolated workerd runner; uploads rehearsal evidence without production access. · PR to `main` touching release admission, deployment preflight, or its workflow/tests · None (`GITHUB_TOKEN` with `contents: read`; no production credentials)
- `research-import.yml` · Runs one research importer (`wikidata`, `sec-edgar`, `companies-house`), or fetches a short list of public pages (`urls`), on a GitHub-hosted runner, because the agents' sandboxes cannot reach those data hosts, and pushes what it wrote to a new branch, `data/<source>-<run id>`. It never writes to a database, never touches `main` and opens no pull request: the branch is reviewed like any other, and the deploy applies a migration only after its PR merges. It refuses a migration number already taken. Every dispatched value reaches the job as an env var and is checked before use, no `${{ }}` sits inside `run:`, and a URL's host must be on its `ALLOWED_HOSTS` list. A fetched page is kept as its text plus the links that may lead to its terms; a CSV is kept as it came; `fetch-log.txt` records each URL, its time and its outcome. Guarded by `frontend/test/research_import_workflow.test.mjs` · manual dispatch, or a `research-import` `repository_dispatch` event whose `client_payload` carries the same three fields: an agent whose GitHub access cannot start a workflow, as the Claude GitHub App cannot, can still send one, because it needs write access to the repository's contents only · none (uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` only, `contents: write` to push the branch)
- `round-call-worker-contracts.yml` · Focused D653/D686 round-call policy, real request/mutation and Raise history contracts with local SQLite and in-app fixture notices; supplements root build and full drift · PR to `main` touching round-call Worker contracts · none (`contents: read`)
- `runner-benchmark.yml` · D5611: branch-only suite benchmark. GitHub is the default. The [CodeBuild runner guide](../../documentation/operations/CODEBUILD_RUNNER_6724.md) covers the optional AWS trials, budget and readiness flags.
- `schema-rehearsal.yml` · #4591: provision a throwaway EU D1 from the committed files, seed synthetic fixtures, export and restore it into a second throwaway D1, compare, and delete both. Never reads or writes production. `documentation/operations/SCHEMA_DRIFT.md` §5 · manual dispatch only · `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (needs **D1:Edit** to create and delete databases), `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`; repository secrets.
- `semgrep.yml` · Static analysis with public OSS rule packs (`p/default`, `p/security-audit`, `p/secrets`). **Findings do not fail this job** — the stripped SARIF is uploaded to code scanning (D718) and `scripts/sarif-summary.py` lists them in the job summary (D672), and ~40 stand. A scanner that could not run *does* fail it, and then nothing is reported, because a crashed semgrep still writes a resultless SARIF that would read as a clean scan (D170). Scanner pinned by digest; the rule packs are still fetched live · main push and weekly; PR security-sensitive paths or `security-scan` (D5602) · Main-push fingerprints retain a baseline and update one redacted scan incident (D5602). Owner confirms scan checks are not required on all PRs. None. To switch on Semgrep AppSec Platform integration (paid), set `SEMGREP_APP_TOKEN` and change `semgrep scan` to `semgrep ci`.
